name: WAITLISTIZE
author: Nemokapitany

sections.description:
Keep bookings moving, even when your events fill up

A full workshop or class should be good news. But when someone cancels, an empty seat can mean lost revenue and another round of messages to manage. Waitlistize helps you take bookings, manage demand and refill available places through a structured waitlist process.

Start with the Waitlistize web app before installing this plugin. We strongly recommend exploring its free booking options and plans to see what fits your business. The Free plan supports individual appointment booking for one consultant and one service. If you organize workshops or group events, explore the guided group-event trial and the plans that offer waitlist management.

Make your WordPress site part of the booking experience

The free WAITLISTIZE WordPress plugin connects your website to your Waitlistize account, so visitors can book without leaving your site to find a separate booking form.

  • Accept individual appointments and group-event bookings through native WordPress booking widgets.
  • Show your services in a service catalog and let visitors choose what to book.
  • Add booking to pages with blocks or shortcodes, using your existing WordPress content.
  • Handle full sessions and waiting lists according to the booking rules and capabilities of your Waitlistize plan.
  • See bookings in WordPress in a read-only overview; open Waitlistize to manage them.

More bookings, less manual chasing

Waitlistize is more than an appointment calendar. When demand exceeds capacity, its waitlist workflows can help move people into newly available places, according to your chosen settings and subscription plan. The web app remains your control center for cancellations, approvals, rescheduling and waitlist operations; this plugin brings the booking experience to your WordPress visitors.

Explore Waitlistize and its free booking possibilities, create your account, then connect it to WordPress.

The plugin itself is free. A Waitlistize account is required, and available booking and waitlist features depend on the selected SaaS plan. There is no separate paid plugin upgrade or plugin license key.

External service and privacy

This plugin connects to the external Waitlistize service, which provides availability, booking processing and account management. See the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.

Connecting a WordPress site sends its site name, HTTPS address, installation and client identifiers, target account identifier and requested permissions to Waitlistize for approval. Once connected, the plugin exchanges account and service information, available booking times, and booking-list data with Waitlistize.

When someone books, the plugin sends the selected appointment or event and the booking details (including name, email, required phone information and consent choices where applicable) to Waitlistize. Anti-spam information, including form timing, honeypot and visitor IP address/user agent, is also forwarded. Waitlistize processes and stores bookings and handles applicable notifications. The plugin does not store a separate WordPress booking database. Only authorized WordPress administrators can view the read-only booking overview, which includes customer information.

Disconnecting removes the site’s local connection credentials and requests remote revocation. If remote revocation cannot be confirmed, revoke the connection in Waitlistize Settings > Integrations > WordPress.
sections.installation:
1. Create or select your plan in the Waitlistize web app. You can start with free individual appointment booking; check the plan options for group events and waitlists.
  2. Install and activate WAITLISTIZE on a WordPress 6.5+ site with PHP 8.2+, Sodium, HTTPS and outbound HTTPS access.
  3. Go to WAITLISTIZE > Settings. Enter your Waitlistize account slug (from the account login URL) and start connecting.
  4. Follow the approval link, sign in to the correct Waitlistize account, verify the site information and approve the connection.
  5. Add a Waitlistize Booking or Service catalog block to a page, or use a shortcode from Services and embeds. Choose your service, publish and test a booking.
  6. Use Bookings for the read-only overview and open Waitlistize when you need to manage or change a booking.
sections.faq:
Is WAITLISTIZE free?

Yes, the WordPress plugin is free. The Waitlistize web app has a Free plan for individual appointment booking with one consultant and one service. Group events and waitlist features are available through trial or paid options. See Waitlistize pricing for the current options.

Can visitors book directly on my WordPress site?

Yes. Add a booking block or shortcode to a WordPress page. The visitor books through your site, while Waitlistize handles availability and booking rules.

What happens when an event is full?

Depending on your Waitlistize plan and configuration, visitors can join a waitlist and released spaces can be filled through manual or automated waitlist workflows. Explore these options in the Waitlistize web app.

Can I manage bookings in WordPress?

You can view and filter bookings from your connected account. To approve, cancel, reschedule or manage waitlists, follow the link to your Waitlistize account.

Do I need a Waitlistize account?

Yes. Create one in the Waitlistize web app, then authorize the WordPress connection from that account.

Can I use WordPress.com?

Only on WordPress.com sites that allow plugin installation and meet the technical requirements. Compatibility with every WordPress.com plan has not been verified.

Do existing connections need to be updated for the booking overview?

Older connections may not have permission to read bookings. If the Bookings screen requests it, disconnect and reconnect to approve the additional permission. Your existing booking widgets can continue working with their existing permissions.

How are interface translations installed?

WordPress installs available community language packs through its standard update system. The booking widget includes Hungarian, English and German labels; some plugin administration and editor text may remain in English until the corresponding language pack is available.
sections.changelog:
0.2.0

  • Native weekly single and group booking UI, backend default resource, consent and service redirect handling.
  • Read-only account bookings with filters, native booking/waitlist identity and safe admin links.
  • Overview, diagnostics and defaults for new blocks; no changes to existing block attributes.
  • Updated HU/EN/DE translations, privacy documentation, reproducible ZIP and release checks.
  • Use WordPress.org language packs for PHP, admin JavaScript and block editor translations; preserve translation sources outside the release ZIP.

0.1.1

  • Target account slug required for pairing; preserve established connections and account renames.

0.1.0

  • Plugin foundation, explicit account approval, encrypted per-site credentials and connection lifecycle.
